Sokyryany Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernivetska oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Sokyryany's Jewish population reached a majority of the town — 5,042 people, 56.1 percent — by 1897, and the town later absorbed thousands of refugees fleeing pogroms in Ukraine during 1918-20, many of whom later emigrated to the US. On October 3, 1941, an extraordinary 30,000 Jewish prisoners held at the Sokyryany camp were expelled to Transnistria in a single action — among the largest such camp populations documented in this collection. About 500 Jews survived the war.
